messages:
srebot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: elevated 5xx rate seen for control-plane config propagation -> dataplane divergence in us-east-1. Alert: CONFIG_SYNC_ERRORS > 3% over 5m. Root thread created 1769004321

maria: seeing customer-facing symptom: Console shows older model version for some hosts while API returns the newer one. Multiple customers reported inference failures.

aj: on it. are we confident this is propagation delay and not a model rollout bug? any recent deploys?

maria: build/deploy window 1769002000 had a canary of config-dispatcher. but the dispatcher reports success for all nodes. logs look noisy.

kai: grabbing logs now. can someone paste the exact error patterns?

rachel: quick customer impact: ~12 active customers in us-east-1 saw token generation errors (502/504) in last 10m. Support alerted 3 paying accounts.

maria: initial mitigation: we toggled feature flag `propagate_async=true` -> `false` for the region to force synchronous propagation. will report effect in 30s.

ops-bot: action log: set_feature_flag(region=us-east-1, propagate_async=false) by maria at 1769004390

aj: good. also add temporary route to fallback control-plane endpoint (cp-fallback-1) for reads. I'll open the route now.

eng-ryan: posting relevant log snippet from config-dispatcher (masking some ids):

```
[1769004352] WARN config-dispatcher: publish_ack_timeout node=worker-23 seq=1874
[1769004352] ERROR config-dispatcher: failed_publish node=worker-42 err=\"connection reset by peer\"
[1769004353] INFO config-dispatcher: retrying publish seq=1874 backoff=200ms
[1769004355] ERROR config-dispatcher: publish failed after retries node=worker-42
```

kai: patterns: worker-42 is the same host group that reported heavy GC last week. could be transient connectivity from that pool.

maria: timeline so far (in-thread build):
- 1769002000 deploy: config-dispatcher v1.9.2 canary (10% hosts)
- ~1769003600 gradual rollout to 100% over 20m
- 1769004320 alert triggered CONFIG_SYNC_ERRORS > 3%
- 1769004352 first publish timeout observed in logs
- 1769004390 feature flag toggled to synchronous propagate

aj: hypothesis 1: dispatcher v1.9.2 has a regression in ACK handling causing retries that expose flaky network links -> delayed propagation -> console/API divergence.

kai: hypothesis 2: control-plane cache invalidation not firing for a subset of nodes (worker-42 pool) due to race with the new async path. need to inspect cache-invalidate logs and redis pubsub.

rachel: quick check: any errors in the dataplane-side consumer? especially the config-applier logs on api hosts.

eng-ryan: pasting dataplane applier error snippet:
```
[1769004360] ERROR config-applier: received config_version=1874 missing dependencies, http_status=502
[1769004361] WARN config-applier: reconnecting to control-plane node=cp-6 err=\"timeout\"
```

maria: mitigation status: after toggling the flag, we see CONFIG_SYNC_ERRORS drop to ~0.7% in the last 30s but still see ~2 hosts with repeated failures.

ops-bot: metric snapshot (us-east-1): CONFIG_SYNC_ERRORS: 3m_avg=0.9% (down from 4.8%) | 5xx_rate_api: 1.2% | console_mismatch_count: 18

aj: next step: isolate worker-42 pool. I'll cordon it from receiving new config publishes and re-route to cp-fallback-1. schedule a restart on that pool after we stabilize.

kai: I'll gather full logs for worker-42 and redis pubsub timelines and paste to the incident doc. pulling now.

maria: customer comms: @support-team please send a brief to the 3 impacted accounts: brief description, mitigation in progress, ETA for full resolution ~30-60m. rachel, can you own that?

rachel: on it. drafting now.

eng-ryan: copied a larger log excerpt to the temp storage link: https://internal.redwood/tmp/incident/1769004321/logs (access restricted)

kai: data we need for RCA: exact message ids of publish attempts, redis pubsub ack timestamps, network error windows, and per-host memory/GC around 1769004300-1769004400.

maria: taking an action item list:
- aj: cordon worker-42 pool + route to cp-fallback-1 (in progress)
- kai: collect logs & redis traces, upload to incident storage
- eng-ryan: collect config-dispatcher traces and retries, correlate with deploy events
- rachel: customer comms and support ticket triage
- maria: keep watch on metrics and decide on rollback if errors don't fall below 0.5% in 10m

aj: cordon done at 1769004510, route applied. one node (worker-42-3) still showing failing ack due to TCP reset; marking for restart.

ops-bot: action log: cordon_pool(pool=worker-42) by aj at 1769004510

kai: uploaded redis pubsub trace and per-host GC summary to incident storage: https://internal.redwood/tmp/incident/1769004321/traces

eng-ryan: correlation note: the failed publish seq=1874 had 7 retries over 2.1s. we see concurrent client reads that timed out around the same period.

maria: immediate result: end-user errors falling, console/API mismatch count decreasing. still tracking a small tail.

aj: proposing rollback plan if stabilization doesn't continue: rollback dispatcher to v1.9.1 in us-east-1 only, keep feature flag synchronous until next patch. rollback would take ~15m with a small risk window. thoughts?

kai: +1 on rollback if tail persists. but prefer deeper log correlation first to avoid churn. if we can identify the exact packet resets and root cause (network or code) rollback is safer.

rachel: customer update sent: included temporary workaround and ETA 60m. customers acknowledged.

maria: handing off after stabilization: aj, can you take the follow-up on the restart + rollback decision? I need to jump to another pager. I'll leave notes here for the post-incident RCA.

aj: taking handoff. I'll continue watch and update thread.

oncall-bot: handoff recorded: from maria -> aj at 1769004790, escalation window 60m

kai: for the in-incident RCA doc we should track: timeline, hypotheses, logs (with links), mitigations applied (flags/cordon/routes), customer impact summary, and final decision (rollback or patch). I'll start a Google doc and drop link here after the runbook template.

maria: final in-thread note before leaving: please capture the exact config flag names and the sequence numbers (1874) — those are critical for the postmortem. Also tag networking team if we find TCP resets correlate with infra.

aj: acknowledged. restarting worker-42-3 now (ssh -> sudo systemctl restart config-dispatcher) at 1769004860

eng-ryan: restart completed, monitoring for new publish attempts.

ops-bot: node_restart(node=worker-42-3) by aj at 1769004872

kai: metrics 5m later: CONFIG_SYNC_ERRORS 0.4% | console_mismatch_count: 3. still watching.

aj: keeping watch. will escalate rollback if we see >0.5% sustained. next update in 10m or sooner if regress.

rachel: leaving support on follow-up with customers, will update if they see anything else.

maria: thanks team. I'm OOO on this one, tagging for follow-up: @eng-sre for RCA and @networking for possible infra blips.

aj: closing live mitigation loop for now. adding notes to incident doc and will draft timeline+hypotheses for RCA.

srebot: incident state: mitigated (partial) — monitoring. Incident thread 1769004321 will be converted to P0 RCA doc when assigned.

kai: created RCA doc draft: https://docs.redwood/r/incident-1769004321-rca (will add logs + timeline).

aj: last_message_ts set to 1769004975 — handing this to the postmortem backlog.
